headlines.title: Chewy vs. Uber Technologies: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
headlines.summary: Chewy has a loyal customer base and a promising pet health pivot. Uber has scale, diversification, and free cash flow growing across three platforms simultaneously.

headlines.title: Why Is Uber Technologies (UBER) Back In Focus After Its $15 Billion Deal Progress?
headlines.summary: Uber Technologies (NYSE:UBER) has moved a step closer to acquiring Delivery Hero in a US$15b deal. Delivery Hero’s management and supervisory boards have recommended that shareholders accept Uber’s offer. The proposed transaction would extend Uber’s delivery footprint to 99 markets, creating a larger global logistics and delivery network. Uber’s US$15b Delivery Hero bid progressing with board backing is one factor to weigh against the rest of our findings.

headlines.title: Uber faces growing AV competition but BofA sees limited market share erosion
headlines.summary: Bank of America (BofA) has maintained its 'buy' rating and $101 price target on Uber Technologies Inc (NYSE:UBER, XETRA:UT8), saying autonomous vehicle (AV) competition will remain the main theme for the ridesharing sector.

headlines.title: Lucid Just Struck a Partnership With Bolt on Mobility. What This Means for LCID Stock.
headlines.summary: Lucid partnered with Bolt to develop an autonomous-ready platform and deploy up to 25,000 self-driving Lucid EVs across major European cities, lifting shares almost 6% in Thursday's trading.

headlines.title: UBER or GRAB: Which Ride-Hailing Stock Holds More Promise Now?
headlines.summary: Uber's stronger bookings growth, lower P/S multiple and broader global scale underpin its edge in this ride-hailing stock faceoff.

description: Uber Technologies, Inc. develops and operates proprietary technology applications in the United States, Canada, Latin America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Asia Pacific. The company operates through three segments: Mobility, Delivery, and Freight. The Mobility segment connects consumers with a range of transportation modalities, such as ridesharing, carsharing, micromobility, rentals, public transit, taxis, and other modalities; and offers riders in a variety of vehicle types, as well as financial partnerships products and advertising services. The Delivery segment allows consumers to search for and discover restaurants to grocery, alcohol, convenience, and other retailers, as well as order a meal or other items, and either pick-up at the restaurant or have it delivered; and provides Uber direct, a white-label delivery-as-a-service for retailers and restaurants, as well as advertising services. The Freight segment manages transportation and logistics networks, which connects shippers and carriers in digital marketplace, including carriers upfronts, pricing, and shipment booking; and offers on-demand platform to automate logistics end-to-end transactions for small-and medium-sized businesses to global enterprises. Uber Technologies, Inc. has staetegic partnership with Mews to embed ride booking, real-time tracking and integrated billing directly into the Mews platform. The company was formerly known as Ubercab, Inc. and changed its name to Uber Technologies, Inc. in February 2011. Uber Technologies, Inc. was founded in 2009 and is headquartered in San Francisco, California.
